segments.text: Here is the Safeway to use Propeller's Price Bix research page.
Find a current row, match the player, stat and exact line, red direction and confidence,
inspect the supporting evidence and timestamp,
and then verify the same projection inside Price Bix.
If the final match fails, stop.
We will use one real, dated example captured on August 17th, 2026.
This is current Propeller analysis, not a claim that Price Bix offers the same line.
First, open the Price Bix research page and check the visible date.
The page requests current public preview data for NBA, MLB and NHL.
On this capture, MLB had five Propeller research rows while NBA and NHL returned no rows.
Desktop and mobile show the same first row.
Christian Franklin, Baltimore, runs batted in, 0.5.
The displayed direction is under and the model confidence score is 79.
Before reading anything else, pause on those three fields, player, stat and line.
They define the research question.
A different player, different stat or different number is not a match.
Next, read direction and confidence separately.
Under is the side supported by the combined analysis.
79 is the strength of that directional signal for the displayed line.
It is not a 79% win probability.
Now inspect the evidence behind the row.
The dated analysis detail included five agents.
Hitch rate evidence noted a long run of games below this threshold.
Ballpark context leaned under.
Usage produced an under projection.
Market context was neutral.
The injury agent reported that no injury data was available.
That missing injury input matters.
It tells you to check late news and the expected lineup yourself.
Agent evidence explains why the model leaned one way.
It does not remove the need to verify what changed after the analysis ran.
Then check freshness.
The source analysis timestamp for this row was August 17th at 2030 UTC.
The public page in both captures used the same dated row.
A response generated later does not make the underlying analysis newer,
so use the analysis timestamp, not just the page load time.
Now perform the prize picks line check.
Open the current player picks board and search for the same player and stat.
Compare Christian Franklin runs batted in 0.5.
Do not match by player name alone.
For this production capture, Propeller's platform backed prize picks end point
returned no records.
The analysis record also identified its market source as underdog, not prize picks.
So the exact projection could not be verified in prize picks.
That is not a reason to substitute a similar line or reuse an older screenshot.
It is the answer.
No verified match means no action from this row.
On mobile follow the same order.
Confirm the date, player, stat and line.
Read the direction and confidence.
Open the detailed evidence.
Check missing inputs and the analysis time.
Then compare the actual prize picks projection on the final screen.
If the line moves from 0.5, if the stat type differs, if the player is unavailable,
or if the projection is missing, the original research question no longer matches.
Refresh Propeller or choose another current row.
The page is a starting point for research, not a shortcut around verification.
Propeller is independent, does not submit entries and does not guarantee outcomes.
The safest workflow is simple.
Exact row, inspectable evidence, honest freshness, actual platform check,
and stop when they do not agree.
